title: Membranes and cysts form only after protoplasm rounds up with positive surface tension

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Membranes and cysts form only after protoplasm rounds up with positive surface tension

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because adsorption requires a surface tension greater than zero, films or threads of creeping protoplasm do not form an encysting membrane, and an organism forms its cyst or cell-wall only when its protoplasm has developed a positive surface tension and gathered into a roughly spherical body.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VI: A Note on Adsorption

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It is for this reason that films or threads of creeping protoplasm shew little tendency, or none, to cover themselves with an encysting membrane; and that it is only when, in an altered phase, the protoplasm has developed a positive surface tension, and has accordingly gathered itself up into a more or less spherical body, that the tendency to form a membrane is manifested

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VI, “A Note on Adsorption”; topic “Encystment and surface tension”. Scope: amoeboid and plasmodial protists that encyst

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch06-03: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.50

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A longitudinal test has clear variables and falsification by wall formation before rounding. Current open imaging may show individual encystment sequences, but not the required simultaneous tension and deposition data across the stated scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track cell shape, cortical tension, and membrane or cyst-wall deposition through encystment and test whether deposition starts only after positive tension and rounding.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The universal 'only when' condition requires broad taxonomic sampling.

Public time series rarely combine tension measurements with wall-formation markers.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The observable pattern, no cyst on a creeping film and a cyst after rounding, is recorded for several laboratory protists. Direct surface-tension measurements are almost never paired with those films. Existing observations can check the morphological sequence in a small subset and cannot separate the tension mechanism from other encystment programs.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare encystment or wall deposition in amoeboid and plasmodial protists while the cell is still a creeping film with the same events after it has rounded. Cysts or walls forming only on rounded cells would support the claim; membranes secreted by still-flattened or streaming protoplasm would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Time-lapse of encystment is public for a few species such as Acanthamoeba and Dictyostelium, not for amoeboid protists generally.

Rounding and encystment can be co-triggered by a developmental switch, so their coincidence does not isolate positive surface tension as the requirement.
